text_fidelity_a:
Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator I've been a Magellan user for several years - have owned four of their GPS systems, and always appreciate how they have improved their products. This unit is my 5th, and replaces a Magellan 4040. After using it for a while I've confident in saying this is the best one yet!

The most visible change is the actual size of the unit. The screen size has been increased, but the unit is thinner and lighter. Very sleek appearance, and the screen is a real joy -- sharp, clear graphics even in the sun, and bigger on-screen buttons for easy use. The mounting system has also been streamlined, and looks and works well. It mounts very easily on a NavMat holder (basically a bean-bag system that I got on Amazon. I'm a huge Navmat fan - makes it a snap to hide the GPS with narry a trace. Best accessory by far for any GPS).

The power connector was not well thought out, however. You have to connect it to the GPS unit AFTER you mount it in the holder. They should have moved the connector it a wee bit to the side to avoid that.

The only button is a slide-type power button on the top. Boot-up time is OK -- not speedy, but not a huge delay either. It does not have a "sleep" mode, so you have to do a cold boot every time. Not a problem in real world use - by the time you get situated in your car, the unit is ready to go.

Voice is clear and easy to understand. Not as natural sounding as a TomTom, but understandable.

Pretty much any recent GPS unit will get you where you want to go. I've found the routing on the Magellans to be very similar to Garmins - could be because they both use the same mapping set (Navteq). The Magellan shines, however, in features that I find helpful. The direction of the next turn is always visible regardless of how far away the next turn will be. Up until recently, Garmin did not offer this (they do now on some of their units). Sounds like a small issue, but I find it very helpful. The Magellan also allows you to very easily exclude a route (or portion). That's a fairly standard feature nowadays, but Magellan allows you to do it in a snap.

In terms of routing, Magellan offers four options (fastest, shortest, most use of freeways and least use). You can see all four options on the map (as a summary) at the same time so you can pick the best one for your needs. Perfect!!

Love the AAA Guidebook, which is a unique Magellan feature. Lets you get details about restaurants and other points of interest just like the paper version from AAA. I used it a lot in my 4040, especially when traveling out of town.

Other unique Magellan features I appreciate is the "ding dong" sound right before a turn (incredibly accurate!) and the fact that the software reminds you to "stay on the current road" when you encounter major exits. Some find that to be nagging, but it has saved me from inadvertently exiting on more than one occasion.

A new feature for Magellan is the lane guidance. Very nicely done. I've used this feature on Navigon units, and found it rather unhelpful. Magellan's implementation is far more useful, with better, clearer graphics. However, lane guidance is not available for every road.

The software is also nicely done - very logical to use. If you're a past Magellan user you can pick this up and use it in a second. If not, there's a short printed user's guide in the box (plus a CD-ROM with more in-depth info) that gets you up to speed quickly. The box also includes the mount, power connector for the car, and a USB cable. It does not include an AC adapter.

OK, now for the bad news. When it comes to customer service, Magellan has been horrid. We're talking so bad it's almost funny. I'm hoping this situation will change - the company was bought by Mitac late last year, and perhaps this will signal a change for the better in terms of customer support. Lord knows, they couldn't get any worse.

The leader, in my opinion, for customer support is Garmin. They are nice to deal with on the phone, answer emails promptly, and offer regular firmware updates. Whenever I buy a GPS as a gift I always buy Garmin since I don't want to saddle the recipient with the miserable service that Magellan offers. It's a shame, since Magellan offers some real benefits over Garmin, and more value for the money. Tom Tom is also decent when it comes to support, but they use TeleAtlas maps which are less complete than NavTeq (sp?).

Bottom line -- if you're looking for a straightforward GPS at a good price, this should be on your short list. It lacks features such as Bluetooth and an MP3 player, but for me, I want a GPS to offer guidance and not entertainment. This has a very robust feature set, great screen, and well-designed software. It also has traffic capabilities -- did not test that feature out, so I can't comment on it.

The "safe" bet continues to be Garmin. You'll pay a bit more, and get less features, but you can be assured of solid support. Whether Magellan's new owners will put them back on the right track (if you'll excuse the horrid, but unavoidable pun) in terms of customer service is not yet clear. I hope so -- they make a great product!

UPDATE: 5/21/09 There's a firmware update on the Magellan site. No new functionality (in terms of new features) but, according to the release notes it improves overall performance. Easy to install - just follow the included step-by-step instructions. It seems like it makes the unit a bit faster, but that could just be my imagination.
text_fidelity_b: Magellan RoadMate 1470 4.7-Inch Widescreen Portable GPS Navigator

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black Build and Setup:
This is a very solid remote. Well constructed. It takes a disk watch type battery that is activated when you remove the tab. The lines are clean and elegant, and it feels well constructed.

Set up was very simple. I simply logged into myharmony.com and choose the Add a remote option.

The difference between this remote and other Harmony remotes is that this has a hub and blaster units that connects through your wireless network to allow you to connect and control your units with your smartphone.

You have to connect the hub and blaster unit around the units you want to control. It has to be connected to your home wireless network, which was easy. You can either do it through myharmony.com or by pressing the setup button on the hub and your router (if it supports it) it was that easy.

This particular unit controls my TV, Dish DVR, and VCR/DVD combo. Setting it up for the units was quite easy.

Using the Remote:
One selling point this has over the Ultimate is that the number buttons are solid state buttons, unlike the touch screen buttons on the Ultimate. As much as I like the touch screen technology, having buttons you can press by touch is a plus for.

There are also traditional DVR buttons, fast forward, as well as red, blue yellow, and green buttons. Since this remote did not have a 30 second advance button, and I rely on that, I programmed a short press of the green and yellow buttons to act as the skip forward. I programmed long pressing those buttons to do the default actions of those buttons. I appreciated that you could customize in that way.

Phone App:
The phone app for the android is a bit lacking as it is not quite as sophisticated as the remote itself, but can do most of the actions of the remote as long as you are connected to the same wireless network as your hub is.

Troubleshooting:
The remote is easy to use and troubleshoot, Simply rebooting or re-syncing the remote can resolve most problems I've found. It also prompts you for assistance the first time you add an action or new device.

Overall this is a great remote. This will demand, though, some knowledge on your part as it is a very sophisticated remote. Many problems that occur can easily be resolved by some knowledge of networks, remotes, or Harmony devices in general. If you have experience with this you will enjoy the functions and capacity of this remote.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone App and Simple All in One Remote - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H Though I received this Acer Chromebook for review, I have another one exactly like it that I bought refurbished about a month ago and have been using it a lot. They are both the same make and model. What I like:

1. The battery life is exceptionally long. I can get a long play list going and it will run all night with nearly a full battery in the morning. I'm using Bluetooth earbuds and I darken the screen so I'm sure that helps to save on battery power.
2. Connects quickly with all my Bluetooth earbuds (and I have several). Only one set of earbuds won't connect and I am still trying to figure that out.
3. Boots up quickly - very short wait time.
4. Screen is nice and big and easy to see.
5. Touchpad works great.
6. Keyboard feels good to use and I'm a very fast typer.
7. It was easy to get it started and on-line right out of the box. It didn't ask me for a billion passwords.

What could be better:
1. Sound is rather weak and really not very good.
2. Screen quality (color, brightness, clarity, etc....) is average
3. Seems to be kind of slow going from site to site....my desktops are much faster.
4. It seems this Acer chromebook doesn't send a Bluetooth signal (weaker) as far as my old Haier chromebook. If I want to listen to something while in bed I have to move the Acer to the bottom of the stairs so the signal will reach. Never had that problem before.

But, for the price of this chrombook (as of this review it's around $179.00) I think it's an excellent buy. It comes with a power cord (of course) but that's it. It uses the Chrome web browser and all I want it for is to check a few sites, write reviews and cruise Youtube. It would be great for college/high school students and anyone who doesn't mind storing their data in the cloud. My main reason for using Chromebooks is that you don't have to buy anti-virus for them since they can't download any data so working off line is not feasible.

It seems to be constructed well and I'm happy with the refurb, but now hubs can use one to surf the web too.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Laptop Webcam C615 with Fold-and-Go Design, 360-Degree Swivel, 1080p Camera I was able to compare this directly to the Logitech C525. They both have the same "fold and go" design, but I was surprised that the C615 is a bit heavier, and I think a millimeter or two thicker. It's well worth it, because the optics are better, and not just better because the resolution is higher - the quality is simply better.

The tripod mount is a nice addition over the C525, adding versitility in positioning. I suppose this would also help you set it up as a hidden camera, or just keep a pile of dirty laundry out of the view mounting on your laptop might otherwise provide.

As others have mentioned, there is a USB extender, which is nice. However, I would much rather have seen a long (or even a very short) cable provided with a microUSB connection to the actual device, allowing the device to become truly portable, rather than having a nice foldable, portable device with a cumbersome cord permanently attached. The user could then use the same cable they charge their smartphone with. Thankfully, the cord is placed in such a way that allows for full 360 degree rotation.

Note that although you can record 1080 videos with this device, you can only chat in 720 - another consideration if you just want this for Skype or another chat program.

Overall, this is the most appealing webcam on the market to me. The most important thing is that it can be tossed in a bag or pocket with other electronics without having to worry about the lens getting scratched.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Laptop Webcam C615 with Fold-and-Go Design, 360-Degree Swivel, 1080p Camera

Update 9-4-16

There are a few tricks to make using the card easier

1. Make sure to have your camera on and not turning off when you are using the card. Don't let the camera ever go into battery saver mode.

2. Use chrome and not safari if you are using an iphone. Chrome even works better than the app provided by easy share.

3. On your iphone go to settings, cellular, and turn off wifi assist all the way on the bottom. It will prevent the iphone from trying to switch from easy share network to the stronger wifi network you have at home.

Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan The Logitech Cooling Pad N200 is a simple padded platform your laptop rests on to keep the hot underside of the laptop from roasting your legs. It connects to the laptop with a USB plug, and draws power from the laptop to run a 2-speed cooling fan (controlled by a switch located on the USB plug).

The pad works splendidly. The fan makes only minor noise in operation even at the highest speed (no more noise than the laptop's own fans make when they engage), and I am completely protected from the heat from the underside of the laptop. The bottom of the pad is nicely padded and is comfortable in use. I didn't have to adjust my position at any point, as I often have to do with the laptop alone, when I need to shift the underside's "hot spot" to another area of my legs.

I can't speak to how much this drains the laptop battery since I very rarely use my laptop without having it plugged in via an AC adapter (my laptop battery is failing and can't run for long without being plugged into the wall).

If I had one nitpick, I would suggest to Logitech that future models have some sort of attachment feature that would allow the laptop to be securely attached to the pad. At present the laptop just rests on top of pad, with the USB connector serving as the only connection between the laptop and the pad. I'd like them to be more securely attached to one another so it's less cumbersome to carry the laptop to another room. But that is a minor issue, and I am otherwise very pleased with this.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Cooling Pad N200 with USB-Powered 2-Speed Fan

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

Initially I was a little disappointed with the Paperwhite because of my own lack of patience and constant comparing it to my other devices. I had to get use to swiping the screen to wake it up, understand the basic settings operations, and generally become comfortable with this model. I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

I am so glad that I did. My only complaint is that I wish Amazon would have included some kind of cheat sheet to get users started. It would have gone a long way to prevent my initial meltdown. If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC3200 Wireless Wi-Fi Tri-Band Gigabit Router (Archer C3200) The router is amazing... Great speeds and looks visually appealing in a room. It has enough processing power that it is able to route data to many wired and wireless device simultaneously and not have any slow downs and the 6 flip out antennas allow the device to have plenty of range to reach even the far corners of the house.

The 3 bands of wireless signal are great, it consists of 1, 2.4ghz network, and 2, 5ghz networks, so that you can assign wireless traffic it's own separate band in order to prevent congestion of a single band.
Remember that a 2.4ghz band will reach further but will be slower, while a 5ghz band will be significantly faster while not reaching as far.

For the more advanced people out there, there are plenty of options that you would expect from a mid range router like this, custom DNS servers, MAC address blocking, port forwarding, DHCP fine tuning, and it also allows you to plug in a USB flash drive into the USB port to use as a small NAS.

The user interface is also quite nice, it is visually appealing and very modern, while retaining functionality and still having the advanced features available for the people who need it.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Bose SoundTouch 10 is an excellent system that enables you to have music, podcasts, and audiobooks available at the press of a button in any room with wifi.

The sleek black design is compatible with almost all decors, and is small enough to hide in a corner.

You can access your content via preset buttons on the top of the device or by using the remote.

Set up was easy at first and then got complicated because my PC was connected to the internet both through wifi and cable. Clearly, the cable was unnecessary, but I didn't know that. You only need one connection. I initially set up the system through my ipad air which was intuitive and only took about 10-15 minutes. The reason I had to contact customer support was I wanted to sync my iTunes library to the Bose SoundTouch. The person I spoke with was patient, knowledgeable, and solved the problem. (And, waiting for tech support only took about a minute.)

I tried the sound qulaity with both classical music and PBS news. The music sounded resonant and rich and had plenty of volume. The speech was clear and easy to understand.

NOTE: Day two. Apparently, my iTunes library is so vast (17,000 items) that it was hard to keep it synched with the Bose system. I could have synched it through Bluetooth, but that meant having to remember to Bluetooth on and off via my desktop, and I use the sound on that all the time; so, it wasn't a viable option. Another idea would be to spend $80 for a NAS drive but that didn't appeal to me, either. I will buy the 3.5mm male to male cable so I can attach my ipod directly to the speaker. It will do the trick, but is not the seamless experience I was hoping for.

I can still listen to radio stations from around the world, i Heart Radio, Pandora, and anything that's downloaded through iTunes on my ipad.

This is a great product if you use it with Bluetooth, or don't have an extensive iTunes library to sync.

I hope to have it as long as I have had my Bose radio, which is more years than I can remember.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech M705 Marathon Wireless Mouse – Long 3 Year Battery Life Ergonomic Sculpted Right-Hand Shape Hyper-Fast Scrolling and USB Unifying Receiver for Computers and laptops Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE (3/30/2019):

This mouse is still functioning as when it was new. I have replaced my 10-year-old Mac Pro with the 2018 Mac mini. I am still using the original Apple Cinema Display. The Logitech Control Center app was installed so the M705 / Marathon mouse would function properly. From time to time I have to unplug the unifying receiver and reinsert it to regain full access to the mouse and its correct assignments of the buttons.

NOTE: There is a newer version of the M705 mouse that does NOT have the side button (left side next to the thumb). The price I paid was $20 recently, but I have not used the newer version yet since this one that HAS the side button still functions.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (November 13, 2017 ):

This mouse was bought to replace the 4-year-old Logitech Performance Mouse - rechargeable battery - because the mouse acted erratically due to lint and other debris that got into the space between the bottom and the plastic covers over the buttons. It prevented drag-and-drop when it would disconnect while dragging. Sometimes the file being moved ended up in another folder that meant I had to UNDO the move and start over. What a pain.

(I began buying Logitech mouse designs after spending too much - $80 - for the Microsoft M6000 laser mouse that was terrible.)

The duration of the parallel battery design makes it last a longer time - I have not had to replace the original batteries yet, but I have been using this only since March of this year (8 months).

The pointer has a tendency to become up to 5 times larger if I move the mouse quickly back and forth left and right. I don't know if this is the mouse or the computer software. I find this interesting, but it does not concern me so I have not asked if anyone else has had the same experience.

One star has been deducted because the scrolling wheel can be used to move up or down the window I am viewing but the window jumps back to where I started. It does not do this all the time, but when I want to scroll up or down to see what has been displayed, it is a pain to have it jump back down or up to where the page had been.

The weight of the mouse is irrelevant when one uses the mouse. It stays on the mouse pad / surface just fine. I am not sure why someone would object to having a second battery in this mouse. For those who have forgotten any high school physical science, the parallel arrangement maintains the 1.5 volts of a single battery but doubles the capacity / run-time of one battery.

As for the mouse specifications: (height x width x depth): 2.6 x 4.3 x 1.6 in; 70.0 x 109.0 x 40 mm (these are from the Logitech site; I would say these measurements are width x length x height considering the way it usually is positioned). Mouse weight: 4.8 oz; 135 g. Compatible OS: Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10, Windows XP, Windows Vista, Mac OS X 10.5 or later, Chrome OS.

For anyone who needs a wireless full-size mouse, I recommend the Logitech M705.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M705 Marathon Wireless Mouse – Long 3 Year Battery Life Ergonomic Sculpted Right-Hand Shape Hyper-Fast Scrolling and USB Unifying Receiver for Computers and laptops Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Jawbone ICON HD - Bluetooth Headset - Black - Retail Packaging Freeway Driving seems to render most headsets useless.
THIS ONE WORKS EVEN ON A NOISY FREEWAY. I did a fair bit of research and read many professional and online reviews looking for a headset that would actually be intelligible to me and to the person I'm calling when I'm on the road. Mostly I use it on the road.

Other headsets got good reviews, and I had tried to find a good one for my iPhone 5. They were fine for indoors and walking, but on the road, voice recognition wouldn't work and I had trouble hearing even road directions from Google Maps.

THIS ONE WORKS and the sound is great. It's a cliche in headset reviews to say that the people you're talking to don't know you're on a headset and say it sounds like a regular phone. For me, this is the first headset where that has been true.

FIT: Fit is always going to be a personal thing. The inside the ear springy loop silicone earpiece works for me. Others are going to need the hook (or both).
I found it to be pretty comfortable, but...

HEAVY AND BULKY: Compared to many headsets (most), this is thick and heavy. It's very noticeably larger and heavier than other headsets I've used. It's not a big problem, but it's not discreet. (That's why they always photograph it so you can't see the thickness)..

BATTERY: I'm not a really heavy user, so I can't say much about talk time. Standby time is noticeably shorter than with other headsets I've used. I haven't measured, but I know I have to charge this significantly more often than my old headsets.

BUT IT WORKS: My old headsets were smaller, lighter, more comfortable and easier to use.
But they didn't work well when I needed them most. I'll take bigger, heavier, and whatnot but WORKS.
text_fidelity_b: Jawbone ICON HD - Bluetooth Headset - Black - Retail Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Armor Suit MilitaryShield Screen Protector For Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I bought this to keep the screen of my roughly $300 tablet safe from scratches. I watched the YouTube instruction video as the included instruction sheet asked. It took me two tries to put the screen on how I wanted it. By that time I had used almost all of the solution. I put the tablet on a dry, dust-free level surface and left it alone for over 24 hours, as instructed.

The screen protector doesn't quite fit the screen (and yes, I bought the correct shield for my tablet). There is a small portion on the left side of the screen that is not covered because the shield is all the way to the right edge of the screen. It has been three days and there are still bubbles under the shield, which makes me think I must have not pushed all the moisture out. The instructions said any imperfections such as micro-bubbles would go away on their own after a couple days. I guess I will see if they do.

The tablet still responds to touching with my fingertips with the shield on. I did notice that when I was using the tablet after installing the shield and waiting the specified time for it to dry that it was difficult to remove little bits and pieces of whatever debris from the environment falls on the screen. Wiping it away takes more effort because things seem to stick to the shield.

That said, I will say that the company seems to pride itself on service, which I appreciate. They include a quality microfiber cloth and a little plastic wedge (I don't know how else to describe it) to push bubbles and moisture from under the shield after it is applied, and the solution is in a quality thin, plastic spray bottle. They also really want feedback so it seems they are committed to improving their service. My rating is for the actual product, the installation required, and overall look, not the company itself.
text_fidelity_b: Armor Suit MilitaryShield Screen Protector For Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film

8/15/2020:
In 15 years, I have had 2 laptops crash. And 1 desktop crash in that amount of time. But - I have never lost information. I don't store my information on my desktop or laptop . . . I worked solely off of harddrives. I have used the WD Elements Hard Drives for over 15 years now. I had 1 4tb that I used over and over again to back up my laptop and personal files. As I got busier with work and life . . . fast forward 15 years and I now have 6 of these. I work daily off of 2 of these . . . one has personal files and the other has work files. No delay. I have 2 backups of the original working harddrives - for work and for personal. I back up every single week like clockwork.

I then have 2 backups of the 1st backups. You don't want to be backing up your working harddrive (thereby putting into play your original harddrive and your 1st back up harddrive) . . . so you need a 2nd back up in the event something catastrophic occurs during the back up of your original harddrives. So I have 3 each for work (1 I work off of every day) and 3 each for personal (1 I work off of every day).

I know that I will always have a full set of my work files, my Outlook files and my accounting files.

Yep . . . it's a $600 investment for peace of mind and security of my files . . . and it's a system that works for me . . .

It's always been my opinion that pre-built machines focus on the specs of a few key components and then skimp on the rest. I can't say this machine changed my mind on that, but it is nice for most people, who don't want to figure out how to make their own to have something already together that just works.

So far, I've used it for a few months and haven't had any failures. It's handled software installations, Windows updates, and new hardware with a minimum of errors. The card readers work. The ports are easy to reach. it isn't especially noisy, but it's far from silent. I've used it for mild gaming, some CAD design work with a program that often crashes and is a ram-hog, and general browing and have had no lagging or problems. Seems to work great!

In my haste to get rid of pre-installed software, I removed the software that turns the light in the DELL logo on and off on the front. I had turned it off, but as soon as I rebooted, it came on and stayed that way. The wires don't seem to be easily accessible to unplug it. I don't consider a bright blue glowing logo that defaults to on to be an added value to the customer, but I guess I'm not really surprised.

I got these either for myself to have a pair of cheap earbuds to take places I don't want to have to worry about losing or to send to my son at college so he doesn't have to worry about losing them. text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black) I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black)

text_fidelity_a: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3 I'm terrible at learning languages. I studied French in junior high, high school and a few years in college, but I still had trouble speaking French fluently. I went to Paris a few times and even dated a French native who criticized every word I attempted, so I gave up. Despite this history of failure, I was curious to see if this Instant Immersion French kit would work for me. The box claims that it is just as good, if not better than Rosetta Stone because they refuse to spend as much on advertising. Hmm. I have a hard time believing that advertising is a main reason why Rosetta Stone is popular. The set comes with 4 CDs and the instructions recommend starting with the Ipod audio CD, though the same sheet of instructions say that it should be used as a supplement to the software. As I sampled each disc, I found that the set is really designed less for a serious French student than for a traveler or someone visiting France on business. There is no attempt to teach grammar or language structure, like present or past tense. The lessons all stress memorization and the ability to recognize and parrot standard phrases, remember a good amount of vocabulary (though not the context to use it). I was disappointed to find that it is structured more like a Berlitz language course. Using flashcards and games to learn language is nothing new, and the Oscar Lake game included is absolutely ancient, as I remember this game from 1998. The only "new" thing about this immersion program is the fact it offers an Ipod and interactive DVD option. The interactive DVD was fun to use though the video is low-tech. Also, the quizzes didn't work that well - I had to click my DVD remote arrow buttons several times before it registered my choice. Did all this it work for me? Did my ability to pronounce words improve? So-so. While I enjoyed playing the games and had fun refreshing my memory using the interactive DVD, the kit offers no real revolutionary way to learn language. It all depends on the student and how motivated you are. In that case, I'd probably do well with Berlitz if I'd only tried harder.
text_fidelity_b: (2011 Version) Instant Immersion French Levels 1, 2 & 3

The corded Logitech Trackman has been my favored trackball for years. My cat chewed through the cord, and it eventually stopped working right, so I had to upgrade. Having a wireless trackball has always seemed rather redundant to me; why would you need cordless when you never move it? Well, it's actually quite nice to not fiddle with the cord! I didn't realize how annoying having a tether is until you no longer have it...

At any rate, this trackball is remarkably accurate (I play several games and work with large spread sheets,) and a snap to install. In short, a reluctant customer is very satisfied!

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz S5 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones with Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod I’m a big fan of the Brainwavz S1 (actually all of their headphones – have yet to be disappointed with any of their products). The S1 has been my main set for active use (e.g., workouts, runs, etc.) since the flat cable is very durable and resistant to tangles. The S5 keeps all the good features of the S1 and adds to it – the sound quality is richer and better defined.

That’s not to say the S1 sounds poor – they are quite good, in fact. But the S5 are better. The highs are better defined and the midrange has more punch to it. The bass comes through clearly without moving into the harsh territory when the volume is pushed (as the S1s can do). The overall sound quality is very pleasing.

The build quality seems solid – as solid as the S1 or better. I love the flat cable! I know that’s something that is not appreciated by everyone, but for me it’s been working out wonderfully. Although this (as most other Brainwavz headsets) comes with an excellent hard shell case, I usually tote my earbuds wrapped around my mp3 player in my pocket. Easy to carry; very stressful on the cables and can lead to tangles with round wires. Flat wires, especially those with a thick jacket such as these, survive that abuse with zero problems.

The earbuds themselves are more sleekly shaped than the “can” style of the S1.

Comfort is in line with the customary Brainwavz style, which is to say it’s outstanding. It comes with a wide range of tips to fit pretty much any ear, plus the Comply foam tips (which are my favorite). If fitted properly you end up with zero ear irritation plus excellent sound isolation and bass response.

These are an over-the-ear design much like the S1. I never used that design prior to the S1 and it did take me a little time to get accustomed to it. It became second nature quickly, and the design is a lot more stable when exercising than the conventional in-ear design.

These are more expensive than the S1, but you can hear the difference in price. Still, if you’re looking to keep the cost down a bit, the S1 is an excellent performer as well.

Great sound, great comfort, wonderful cable design, and it comes with a solidly made case and lots of eartips. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz S5 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones with Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod

Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Compact Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Set 2.4G Ultra-Thin Sleek Design for Windows, Computer, Desktop, PC, Notebook, Laptop (Black01) I think this set is very cute in terms of design with some hidden features that is not marketed. So here is what I think.

Build Quality & Design:
I think the color is personal preference, but still think the white-pastel baby pink theme is very cute. Other than that, it doesn't have any unnecessary design element. The finish material is somewhat cheap plastic, but when you consider for $15 keyboard AND mouse set, it is extremely well done. As you can see from photo, they prepared USB-B home on the back, next to battery. Most other companies do that under the mouse, so this was very interesting choice of design. Definitely, it is somewhat inconvenient, if you have to use this set in multiple computer. Other than that, it doesn't bother me at all.

Functionality:
Again, this is somewhat personal preference, this keyboard makes very low hitting sound except the spacebar. I have no idea why they built this way. So it is too much for silence keyboard because of the spacebar but it sounds very dull if you like to hear the mechanical sound of typing. This keyboard doesn't have 6 key island (insert/home/page/delet/end key, normally placed on top of cursor arrows.) If you need for these keys frequently, then this keyboard is not for you. It does have fn-key function so you can use these keys somehow, but it's somewhat inconvenient. Also, they placed backspace twice (one in the conventional place and in the number pad under + sign. This set needs 4 AAA battery, which I think it's a little excessive.

Ergonomics:
Both the keyboard and mouse are very thin, so it feels somewhat inconvenient. Especially the mouse looks and feels very similar to the old apple mouse, adding considerable pressure on wrist. If you are okay with Apple mouse then you will like it. (But not me.)

Buy it if you need : a set of keyboard & mouse with limited budget with extremely cute colors
Don't if you want: ergonomic, full keyboard or if need to use your computer for long time
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Compact Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Set 2.4G Ultra-Thin Sleek Design for Windows, Computer, Desktop, PC, Notebook, Laptop (Black01)

text_fidelity_a:
ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This timer is a good size with a very readable LED display and a strong magnet on the clip on the back to hold it to your fridge or whatever a magnet will stick to. The buttons are large and accessible, and it's really no problem to set it up. It beeps loudly when the time is up, so there's little danger you're not going to hear it from an adjoining room.

Strangely, on day one (unlike with some timers I've used), the first three or four times that I held down the hour, minute, or second buttons to speed up the counting and turn off the beeps, it just froze and stopped counting. If I pressed the button over and over to advance the counter by one, it worked—beeping annoyingly loudly each time, of course. I was about to give it a two-star review and throw it away because I couldn't stand it, but I put off doing it and just stuck it to the top of my stove. A week later, after I'd used the stove several times and the timer probably got exposed to some heat, I went back to try it again so I could write this review and the fast-count sans beeps feature worked. Weird. Maybe it was just stressed in shipping and needed time to settle down....

A few things I really do dislike is that it's easy to reset the time by mistake if the grey button on the left gets slid up; the modes are manually set with this button. (That approach to the modes could be good for the technologically challenged, though.) Also, if you overshoot your mark on the time, there is no way to go backward; you have to go forward until you come back around to where you were supposed to have stopped the first time. The clip is a little too sharply angled, so when you stick the timer to a surface with the magnet, the face slants down somewhat, but it's still visible; really not that big of a deal.

Another thing, as I've remarked about another MeasuPro product: the how-to info on the packaging is white letters on light grey, which is practically unreadable for anyone, not just people like me with old eyes. (The company told me they were correcting that with the other product, so I expect they will do the same with this one.)
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

text_fidelity_a:
Canon PowerShot A1400 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 5x Digital Image Stabilized Zoom 28mm Wide-Angle Lens and 720p HD Video Recording (Black) (OLD MODEL) These cameras are amazing. Get a 32GB chip, put CHDK on it and you can do awesome stuff with this camera. I bought two for my family's trip to Alaska, and we snapped thousands of photos. Very good quality, fair low light performance, controls are easy enough. We spent a fair bit of time learning the controls so we'd be fluent with them.

Here's a neat trick: You can use these cameras as low power microscopes. Put the Macro setting on, take a photo as near ask the thing will focus, which is pretty close, then hit 'Play' and use the zoom lever on the shutter release to zoom in and get a microscope view of what you took the photo of.

Also, with CHDK on the SD card, you have a built in intervelometer for taking time lapse sequences.

Another fun thing to do is to take night time photos of the sky using the long exposure setting. With the 10 second setting and the ISO turned up you can capture images of stars or northern lights in the night sky. Fantastic for a $60 camera.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot A1400 16.0 MP Digital Camera with 5x Digital Image Stabilized Zoom 28mm Wide-Angle Lens and 720p HD Video Recording (Black) (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a:
TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Do not be afraid! This is a great TV.

The good: I won't go into the technical details and explanations. Others have done that for me. We purchased this for a new home and have had it set up for a couple of weeks. The integration of Roku is seamless, and it retains those same intuitive menus. It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

The bottom line: I was skeptical. I've owned Samsung plasma and LED and an LG LED recently and I see no material difference between the TCL and the other LEDs. All the positive reviews here, plus the CNet reviews/primers on Roku integrated TVs put me over the edge. We really like this TV and it's simplified our streaming incredibly. Go get it!
text_fidelity_b: TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405

text_fidelity_a: sympa Desk Lamp, Dimmable Table Lamp with 3 Color Temperatures, 10,000 Lux UV-Free Portable Sun Lamps, Timer & Memory Function, for Home, Office This is a nice light therapy lamp that is very simple to use. The only parts are the lamp itself and a power cord. Once the lamp is plugged in, it’s simply a matter of touching the power button to turn it on, then pressing and holding the brightness button to set the lamp to the desired brightness level. At the highest setting it is very bright, too bright for me if I’m close to the lamp, but nice if you’re lighting up a room. Provided you don’t unplug the lamp after turning it off, the lamp will remember your desired setting and return to that when it’s next turned on. I’ve used other light therapy lamps that have a timer function; this one does not. Others are more portable, being the size of a small tablet or a Kindle. This one is rounder and looks to me more like a room lamp. Depending on how you wish to use the lamp and what functions you’re looking for, this may be a very good fit provided you plan to keep it in one place rather than transport it and don’t need a timer.

The plastic back and seems are very well constructed. The product feels very solid and good quality. The resolution and sound are amazing. It was easy to set up and had all my favorite apps. Android cannot do Amazon instant but I am sure that will come soon. It is light weight and easy to hold and carry. Boots up quickly and very portable. I use my tablet more than my laptop and look forward to using this product. The web browsing is fast and all other apps work great. I have an asus transformer prime but that one is not really multi media but great for school or work. I did not want to pay what I did for the transformer prime and this was a perfect bridge for the price. I like asus products. I would reccomend this tablet.

3/17/2014 update: ASUS just pushed the android 4.3 update. Now my tablet is buggy and it was not before. The internet connection does not work most of the time when I boot up. I have to re-boot several times. the internet just stops working and goes back to the home screen randomly. If I am watching a movie or listening to music the tablet just re-boots randomly. I did not have any of these issues before the 4.3 update this past weekend. I am no longer happy with this product. Buyer's beware until they fix these issue. I plan to message ASUS on their site so they are aware this is happening.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS MeMO Pad FHD 10 ME302C-A1-BL 10.1-Inch 16GB Tablet (Blue)

Sony BDP-S590 3D Blu-ray Disc Player with Wi-Fi (Black) (2012 Model) The setup was easy. I found no trouble, no complications, no issues. I just plugged it in and it works.

It streams Netflix, Hulu, and Amazon videos with no trouble. Setup for those was easy as well. My router is on the fritz, and when too many packets get lost, the device drops the connection (can't blame the device--it can't stream if it can't connect to the Internet) but it recovers smoothly. I've seen other devices just fail and return to the menu. This pauses and picks up where it left off once it is able to reestablish a connection.

The image quality is outstanding. The form factor is beautiful. The interface is easy to use. The remote is a little fatter than most, so expect to give it one of the larger pouches in the remote boat.

It does not contain cables, so pick up good ones. I like [[ASIN:B003L1ZYYW AmazonBasics High-Speed HDMI Cable (9.8 Feet/3.0 Meters) - Supports Ethernet, 3D, and Audio Return [Newest Standard]]] Not all HDMI cables are equal. It depends on which specification it implements (these are 1.4) and what part of the specs the cable implements.

I'm very pleased with this device.

text_fidelity_a: ADATA SU760 512GB 3D NAND 2.5 Inch SATA III Internal SSD (ASU760SS-512GT-C) Laptop is SO MUCH faster. Write and read date are fast too. I haven't upgraded the ROM, but I presume it'll be even faster once I do! Comes with FREE software to clone your old HDD into this. However I would suggest a fresh CLEAN install. I recommend you make two partitions in SSD at least. One for the OS and one for your files. That way if OS fails you can repair, or reinstall, OS into OS partitions and not worry about your Documents in the files partition. I have more partitions because I use LINUX MINT in conjunction with WINDOWS. No issues with that, you just need to be sure of what you are doing when working with MBRs. Works great with WINDOWS 10, LINUX MINT, and OSX..MACHINTOSH...APPLE OS...however you call it. All three OSs ran good on same machine with this SSD.

Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD 2TB NVMe M.2 Internal Solid State Hard Drive, V-NAND Technology, Storage and Memory Expansion for Gaming, Graphics w/ Heat Control, Max Speed, MZ-V7S2T0B/AM Modern computers are a lot more reliable than computers from 10 or 20 years ago. Computers are not getting a lot faster every year like they used to. I no longer replace my computer every couple of years. If your computer is getting a little sluggish, instead of replacing the whole thing, you can usually give it a huge performance boost by upgrading just key components. In particular, upgrade your memory and upgrade your hard drive. This SSD does not add a lot of capacity, but it gives you a lot of speed so that programs or databases that you use a lot will load much more quickly.

This drive installed and formatted easily on my Windows 10 desktop computer. It's been running flawlessly since then and the performance has been blazingly fast.

There are a lot of different SSDs on the market these days. Check your computer manufacturer's website to see what is compatible with your motherboard. This SSD costs 2 to 3 times as much as entry-level products with the same capacity. The more advanced design makes it more than twice as fast as more basic SSDs. If you use your computer for computer-aided design, graphics/video editing, or hard-core gaming, then the speed may be worth the price to you. For general purpose office or home computing, the entry-level SSDs are probably fine for you.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 970 EVO Plus SSD 2TB NVMe M.2 Internal Solid State Hard Drive, V-NAND Technology, Storage and Memory Expansion for Gaming, Graphics w/ Heat Control, Max Speed, MZ-V7S2T0B/AM

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50) Update, Aug 2016: It's been 5 months since I installed this router and it has the distinction of never needing to be rebooted yet! That's a record for me, since some of my past routers needed a reboot every week or two (or even every day or two). I continue to be impressed with the rock-solid performance of this TP-LINK. It's not fancy and lacks some high-end features, but I'll take solid, dependable performance over flash any day.

Original review:
While this router won’t satisfy the needs of those who have complex networking requirements or those who like to tinker and tweak, it offers solid performance, AC speeds and good coverage at a very reasonable price point. If you’re looking to go to AC speed but don’t want all the bells and whistles, this offers a lot for the money.

The footprint is very small compared with other routers I have, which is a nice change. The overall build quality seems very good, and the two antennae are firmly attached (another problem I’ve had with lower-end routers). It has an off switch which is handy if you need to do a reboot. It runs warm but not hot.

Setup is very straightforward if you want to keep the default settings. Basically just plug it into a PC, access the router menu with your browser, set the network name and password, and you’re done. You can access more advanced features if needed, but for a basic setup the time required is less than 5 minutes.

Performance has been impressive. I also have AC routers from D-Link and Linksys that are far more costly than this, but this little guy holds his own when it comes to coverage and throughput. For example, I get Internet connection speeds of about 62mBps with my D-Link DIR-880L. This router, with the same PC and network card, gives me 50mBps. Wireless coverage is a little more spotty with this router on fringe areas (e.g., for a PC located a floor above and at the opposite end of the house from the router) but it still maintains a connection, albeit at lower speeds.

This does lack some features that could be helpful for some situations. It has a USB port, but only has one, and it’s a 2.0 USB port. It lacks a gigabit port as well. But again, for the price, it offers a lot of performance. So far I’ve had zero problems or glitches.

This router won’t excite a power user or satisfy complex networking requirements/demands, but for the basics, it gets the job done with solid speed and performance. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive router.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC1200 Reliable Dual Band WiFi Router (Archer C50)

SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black) When I ordered this, I didn't realize that I would be required to use the screen protector part of it. I thought that I could just slip on the back piece and use it like that. When I realized that both pieces are required (the back is too big and wouldn't stay on without the screen protector piece; hey, it's the first time I've ordered something with an integrated screen protector, so I didn't know), I wanted to send it back without even trying it.

I'm glad that I decided to try it for a couple of days, first. The screen is always covered with fingerprints and smudges and I find myself wiping it off many times a day. It also scratches easily. Since we're all washing our hands 40 times a day, the amount of fingerprints feels excessive to me and I hate looking at it. Even so, with the screen protector on, the screen is very responsive. Zero problems. And while I'm actually using my tablet, I don't notice the scratches or fingerprints.

There is also a shimmery rainbow effect. I don't really notice it while the screen is on and it seems to be less of an effect after the couple of weeks that I've been using it. I think because there's less of an air gap.

Everything lines up perfectly and the back part of the case also seems perfect to me. I would love to see this brand make a version that's just the well-fitted back piece.

So is it perfect? No. However, the things that bother me about it aren't really noticeable while the screen is on and I'm using it. It's protective and the screen protector doesn't interfere in the responsiveness of the screen in any way. So overall, I do think that this purchase was worth it. I'm glad that I decided to try it instead of immediately sending it back.

Another comment -- I keep a little piece of electrical tape over the front camera hole. The screen protector holds the tape in place so that I don't have to periodically change it anymore.
text_fidelity_b: SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung SyncMaster 245BW 24-inch LCD Monitor This is the first high quality 24" I have seen for under $500. Yes, this is one of the new 24" TN (twisted neumatic) panels, but don't let that dissuade you. The 22" TN panels have gotten a bad rap due to their poor performance, most of them have issues with bad color banding and lots of light bleeding at the edges. I should know as I have owned several 22" TN panels (mostly Viewsonic VX2235WM).

This 24" TN panel is far and away superior to any previous TN panels I have seen, it is almost laughable how bad my old 22" TN panel looks up next to this one. I would challenge you to put this 24" TN up against any of the more expensive 24" IPS or S-PVA panels and see the difference for yourself, I doubt you will be able to tell which is which unless you are using a specialized image for gamut testing or you are a graphic designer with an extremely keen eye.

The only downsides that some people may find with this monitor compared to other (usually more expensive) 24" panels are: less inputs, no portrait mode. This monitor only has VGA and DVI(+hdcp) inputs, no component or hdmi, this is not really an issue if you are using it as a computer monitor but may turn off some people who wish to hook up other media devices. Also there is no portrait mode like the other 24" samsung 244T series; however, the stand on this monitor is still extremely high quality and height adjustable.

I would very highly recommend this LCD, better yet, I'd recommend 2 or 3. Why buy a 30" when you could have 3 of these for the same price?!
text_fidelity_b: Samsung SyncMaster 245BW 24-inch LCD Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New) An upgrade of Nikon's original digital-only tele kit zoom, this new 55-200mm f/4-5.6 ($250, street) adds Vibration Reduction and a number of optical improvements for only $70 more. A 3.6X 82-300mm equivalent zoom, it's not expected to be bundled in Nikon DSLR kits any time soon.

Hands on:

The barrel, when contracted, is nearly an inch longer than the earlier 55-200mm non-VR DX lens, but is still extremely light as a result of all-plastic construction, including the lensmount. The large zoom ring's slightly uneven and underdamped turning action is what you'd expect from a lens at this price. The narrow manual-focusing ring is even-turning but also underdamped, with a very short turning radius for fast, if coarse, manual focusing. AF action on our test camera, the D40x, was adequately fast and quiet, thanks to Nikon's Silent Wave Motor in the lens.

In the lab:

SQF tests found Excellent sharpness and contrast at all focal lengths -- an improvement over the earlier, non-VR version of this lens. DxO Analyzer 2.0 tests found Imperceptible barrel distortion at 55mm (0.08%), and Slight pincushion distortion at 105mm and 200mm (0.24% and 0.19%, respectively). All three are also improvements over the earlier lens. Light falloff was gone from the corners by f/5 at 55mm, f/7.1 at 105mm, and f/8 at 200mm.

At the uniform close-focusing distance of approximately 43.5 inches, tests of close-up ability found maximum magnification ratios ranging from 1:14.25 at 55mm to 1:3.8 at 200mm, about an average magnifying power, and not up to the 1:3.4 turned in by the non-VR 55-200mm. DxO Analyzer Blur tests of the lens' first-generation VR system (at 200mm) showed an improvement for three users of about 3 stops of extra handheld sharpness at slower shutter speeds; 4 stops are possible with Nikon's VR II system.

Conclusions:

Even though it's the earlier version of VR, to get any VR at this price is a steal.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens Bulk packaging (White box, New)

text_fidelity_a:
Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer] I was rather surprised when I got this with how small it is. I knew from the product description that it would be a little guy, but didn't have an appreciation for how small it was until I got it. It's a cube that is less than 1.5 inches on each side. Very compact, but it feels very solid and well-made.

Despite the compact size this is a solid performer. The video quality is quite clear and vivid provided you keep the cam steady. That's not easy to do if this is handheld given the small size, but it's designed to be mounted (there's a magnet in the base plus there are a variety of options available for mounting. Note that the mounts are sold separately).

The sound quality is good. Not spectacular, but reasonably clear and on a par with most cams I've used that have an internal mic.

Getting to the SD card is where the small size does cause a problem - it's not all that easy if you don't have nimble fingers (which I do not). You need to open the access door (which is sealed for water resistance) with a coin.

It doesn't have a lot of features which I find to be a plus since it greatly simplifies operation - the interface is a single button that turns it on/off, takes a still or starts/stops video recording. Can't get easier than that!

Minor quibbles aside, this is a solid performer and one that's well worth considering if you're looking for a very unobtrusive cam that's easy to operate (other than getting the SD card in and out). 4.5 stars rounded up to 5 due to the performance at this price point.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Polaroid Cube HD 1080p Lifestyle Action Video Camera (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer]

So I decided to try Amazon on this 2016 Samsung that had many good reviews and was a good price. I was very impressed with both the TV and the delivery from Amazon.
Delivery: I was able to select which day I wanted it delivered and then was kept updated on the delivery status by Amazon. The delivery company called a few days in advance to verify a 3 hour window of time, and they did arrive that day within the window of time even though it was 10 min prior to the end of that time. They brought the TV in, removed it from the boxing, placed it on our TV stand, plugged it in and verified it was functioning. text_fidelity_a:
Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 1 camera kit UPDATE (8/4/2019):
After some recent system updates, I have found that the 5 sec video may not be accessible until after someone has left the area. It was not that snappy before, but now it seems to be slower in accessing the video from my phone.
Additionally, I have had packages put on my front deck / steps that is 10 feet away from my front door and the Blink XT2 camera, but the video was never triggered. The Blink is aimed in that direction. So I have changed the sensitivity from 5 to 9, the highest. Also, I have changed the clip length to 10 seconds. We shall see how this functions.

Since I have had the Blink XT2 less than a week, I will update when I know more about how long the batteries last.

READ THE INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE BEGINNING INSTALLATION.

Download the app first. Once the app is downloaded, it will prompt you as to what has to be done. Use the device to take a photo of (read) the camera’s ID (QR code) OR enter the Serial Number manually.

Open the camera - Remove the back cover by holding down the gray ‘button’ while pulling the bottom of the back cover away from the camera body. It has a rubber or silicone gasket in the groove around the cover. Because it has a friction fit, it can be difficult to pry off the cover. I could put a little lube on the sealing gasket, but it might cause problems if it reacts with either the plastic or the gasket.

All synching has to be done while the camera is open, then it is put together before mounting it. The Sync module has to remain plugged into an AC outlet, so find a convenient place for the module to rest or hang.

The back cover is replaced by pressing it firmly where the posts are located until a ‘click’ is heard near each corner.

I used the base of the mount to locate and drill 2 small holes in the wood. Then I put the screws into the mount and the base and attached the mount to the house. After the base is attached, the cam is pressed onto the mount. That was the hard part.

The mount attaches to the hole in the back cover by pressing the assembled camera onto the mount. This should be done after the mount is attached to the desired location using the two screws included.

I had installed the camera as high as I could above my front door. Most of the videos showed the top of my head, nothing as to identifying me from my face. So I thought I would move it a little lower, still above the door; and as I turned the camera so I could use a long screwdriver to remove the screws, it came off the mount and fell onto the floor. Apparently, it suffered no ill effects. Perhaps the very warm temperatures made the plastic loose enough for it to come off easily. I would like to have a more secure mounting system. I have ordered a mount that has a cover to hold Blink XT2 securely.

At bottom of the Home screen of the app, be sure to slide the switch so that it says Armed.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black
